extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, regulated electric utility owners/operators, environmental regulators, and policy/legal stakeholders involved in CAA section 111(d) state plan development and EPA review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and binding requirements for identifying the Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER), the degree of emission limitation achievable, subcategories, applicability, presumptive standards, compliance dates, and state plan submission content for existing fossil fuel-fired steam generating units under CAA section 111(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA must determine BSER and degree of emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA must 'determine' the best system of emission reduction which has been adequately demonstrated and ascertain the 'degree of emission limitation achievable through the application' of that system; the EPA cannot shift those determinations to the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAA section 111(d) directs EPA to (1) determine the BSER, (2) ascertain the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER, and (3) impose emissions limits that reflect that amount. The preamble criticizes approaches that leave BSER or degree determinations as open-ended for states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for evaluating candidate BSERs
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the BSER for a source category, EPA identifies systems of emission reduction that have been adequately demonstrated and evaluates the potential emissions reduction, costs, any non-air health and environmental impacts, and energy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA uses these factors (adequately demonstrated; emissions reduction potential; costs; non-air health/environmental impacts; energy requirements) to decide whether a control meets BSER requirements and to set associated degrees of limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emission limitation must be sufficiently specific (numeric or bounded)
rubrics_metrics.description: The emission guideline must identify the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER with sufficient specificity; unbounded ranges or effectively unlimited ranges (e.g., '0 to >2%') are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble notes prior emission guidelines included numeric degrees (examples cited) and criticizes ACE for providing ranges and shifting determination to states; EPA must provide a benchmark so states can craft approvable standards and EPA can determine whether plans are 'satisfactory.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance must reflect EPA-determined degree and be no less stringent
rubrics_metrics.description: States' standards of performance must reflect the degree of emission limitation that the EPA determines in the emission guidelines and must contain 'emission standards ... no less stringent than the corresponding emission guideline(s).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation to 40 CFR 60.24(c), 60.24a(c) and CAA section 111(d)(2)(A). EPA retains primary regulatory role and reviews state plans for substantive adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: States must consider remaining useful life (RULOF) when applying standards
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying a standard of performance to any particular source, a state may consider, among other factors, the remaining useful life of the existing source to which such standard applies (RULOF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAA section 111(d)(1) allows remaining useful life as a factor; discussed further in section X.C.2 of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan submission content for candidate-technology approach (ACE Rule procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If using candidate technologies to develop standards, the state must 'evaluat[e] each' candidate technology and provide a summary including an evaluation of the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the technologies and provide specified plant-level data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required plant information includes 'annual generation,' 'CO2 emissions,' '[f]uel use, fuel price, and carbon content,' 'operation and maintenance costs,' '[h]eat rates,' '[e]lectric generating capacity,' and the 'timeline for implementation,' among other information. The ACE Rule required these but did not supply the numeric BSER benchmark itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission control choice must reduce emissions (no counterproductive effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The core element of the BSER analysis is whether the emission reduction technology selected actually reduces emissions; technologies that are counterproductive (i.e., may increase emissions) raise questions about whether they are the 'best.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Essex Chem. Corp. v. Ruckelshaus and points to the 'rebound effect' where heat-rate-improvement (HRI) measures could increase absolute CO2 emissions by displacing lower-emitting sources; EPA concluded BSER must not be likely to increase emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated facility applicability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'designated facility' for these emission guidelines is any fossil fuel-fired electric utility steam generating unit that: (1) was in operation or had commenced construction on or before January 8, 2014; (2) serves a generator capable of selling greater than 25 MW to a utility power distribution system; and (3) has a base load rating greater than 260 GJ/h (250 MMBtu/h) heat input of fossil fuel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT. 'Existing source' definition follows section 111(a)(6); newly constructed or reconstructed units after specified dates are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of exemptions from requirement to establish standards under a state plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EGUs that may be excluded from the requirement include: (1) units subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart TTTT due to qualifying modification/reconstruction; (2) units with federally enforceable permits limiting net-electric sales to ≤1/3 of potential output or ≤219,000 MWh annually (and never exceeded); (3) non‑fossil fuel units with permit limiting fossil fuel use to ≤10% annual capacity factor; (4) CHP units with a permit limiting annual net-electric sales to ≤219,000 MWh or design efficiency*potential output; (5) units that serve a generator with effective generation capacity ≤25 MW (prorated); (6) municipal waste combustors subject to subpart Eb; (7) commercial/industrial solid waste incineration units subject to subpart CCCC; (8) EGUs deriving >50% heat input from an industrial process that does not produce electrical/mechanical output used outside the EGU; (9) coal units that elect to permanently cease operation prior to January 1, 2032.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions mirror many current exemptions in 40 CFR 60.5509(b) and are discussed in detail in section VIII.E.1 of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization by fuel type and relevant characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may create subcategories (e.g., coal-fired, oil-fired, natural gas-fired steam generating units) where sources differ by characteristics relevant to suitability of controls; fuel type, amount combusted, and capacity factor affect control performance and are bases for subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalizes coal, oil, and natural gas subcategories in part based on amount of fuel combusted and other operational characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for long-term coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term existing coal-fired steam generating units (those not medium-term), EPA determines CCS with 90 percent capture of CO2 meets BSER requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of this BSER results in a degree of emission limitation equivalent to an 88.4 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). Compliance date for these sources is January 1, 2032. EPA assessed cost reasonableness assuming long amortization periods and historical cost metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and BSER for medium-term coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: Medium-term coal-fired units are those that have demonstrated plans to permanently cease operations after December 31, 2031 and before January 1, 2039; for that subcategory, EPA determines natural gas co-firing at 40 percent of annual heat input is the BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of 40% co-firing results in a 16 percent reduction in emission rate (lb CO2/MWh-gross). Co-firing entails less equipment and capital cost than CCS and EPA determined it meets cost-reasonableness metrics for units with amortization periods more than 2 years (i.e., those ceasing after Jan 1, 2032 and up to Dec 31, 2038). EPA expects implementation by January 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exemption for units ceasing before Jan 1, 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired steam generating units that demonstrate they plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2032 are not subject to the 40 percent co-firing requirement and are exempted from these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized this exemption because such units have very short amortization periods (2 years or less) and co-firing costs would generally not be comparable to reasonableness metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of amortization period in cost-reasonableness judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs of control technologies (especially capital-intensive CCS) are evaluated relative to the period over which sources can amortize capital costs; shorter remaining operation time increases annualized costs and may change which controls are cost-reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated CCS costs for different amortization periods and created subcategories (long-term vs. medium-term) accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units based on capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: For natural gas- and oil-fired units, EPA finalizes subcategories by annual capacity factor: base load (>=45%), intermediate load (>=8% and <45%), and low load (<8%). For base and intermediate subcategories, BSER is routine methods of operation and maintenance and degree of emission limitation is 'no increase in emission rate'; for low load units BSER is lower-emitting/uniform fuels with degrees defined on heat-input basis (130 lb CO2/MMBtu for natural gas; 170 lb CO2/MMBtu for oil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides presumptive standards (discussed below) and sets compliance date of January 1, 2030 for all natural gas- and oil-fired steam generating units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptive standards of performance for subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides presumptively approvable standards of performance based on the degree of emission limitation achievable through application of the BSER for each subcategory: for base load sources 1,400 lb CO2/MWh-gross; intermediate load 1,600 lb CO2/MWh-gross; low load oil-fired 170 lb CO2/MMBtu; low load natural gas-fired 130 lb CO2/MMBtu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although states establish standards of performance, EPA supplies these presumptive standards as presumptively approvable benchmarks; inclusion in table 1 is for completeness and further discussion is in section X of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates tied to control type and subcategory
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes compliance/implementation dates tied to the chosen BSER and subcategory: e.g., January 1, 2032 for coal CCS (long-term), January 1, 2030 for co-firing (medium-term coal) and for all natural gas- and oil-fired units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates reflect expected time to implement controls (CCS longer/greater infrastructure; co-firing quicker and less capital-intensive).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA reviewability requirement — avoid standardless review
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission guidelines must provide a benchmark and substantive guidance so EPA review of state plans is not a 'standardless exercise'; procedural constraints alone are insufficient to ensure substantive adequacy of state standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cites its longstanding view that review limited solely to procedural criteria is inappropriate because states could set extremely lenient standards that meet procedural requirements but fail substantive goals (40 FR 53342-43 (1975)).

rubrics_metrics.name: NSR revisions tied to BSER rationale and may be withdrawn if BSER changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to NSR applicability (e.g., hourly emissions rate test to ease permitting for HRI projects) were contingent on ACE Rule's HRI-based BSER; with repeal of ACE Rule and change in BSER, the EPA withdraws NSR revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA also notes that NSR applicability serves as a beneficial backstop to review situations where absolute emissions increase following modifications, and that any future NSR proposals should be reproposed with updated justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER selection must account for changed circumstances and updated evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may reexamine and revise BSER determinations based on changed factual underpinnings (e.g., updated technical reports showing lower HRI effectiveness, reduction in costs for CCS and natural gas co-firing, expansion in availability of natural gas, IRA changes to 45Q tax credit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency cites FCC v. Fox for the principle that a new policy need not demonstrate it is 'better' but must be permissible and supported by good reasons; examples: updated Sargent & Lundy report, IRA 45Q changes leading to lower effective costs for CCS.
